svg.text: Distributed Tile DSL + HDA Mega-Device - TileLang Extension - github.com/tile-ai/tilescale
L1 - Distributed AI Workloads (intra-chip + inter-chip unified programming)
L2 - Hierarchical Distributed Architecture (HDA) - unified mega-device virtualization
Compute units - Memory layers - Network links
Hierarchically grouped at each scale level
thread - warp - warpgroup - block/SM - cta_cluster - device - node
Levels HW-defined - names vary per architecture
L0 register/fragment - L1 shared - L2 cache
Shared or distributed per compute unit at each scale
Inter-node IB - software channels via lower mem
Not locked to specific HW vendors
L3 - Hierarchical Tile Programming Interface (consistent primitives at every scale)
Multi-scale tile view: block to thread reg
Software channels when no HW link exists
Same op at high scale = lower-scale impl group
L4 - Frontend (Python DSL + TileLang base + hierarchical syntax extensions)
L5 - Middle Layer (Compiler + Tile Kernel Library + Cost Model)
Lower frontend program to IR + optimization passes
Lower high-scale tile primitives to lower-scale ops
Schedule compute + comm + memory access overlap
Layout inference for multi-scale T.view partitions
Select best impl variant via cost model feedback
Pre-implemented tile primitive kernels at each scale
Block-scale GEMM direct map OR recursive lower
Default impl per primitive (TMA vs LSU vs CE)
Lightweight feedback for compiler tuning decisions
Impl selection: copy engine vs TMA vs remote path
L6 - Backend Module (configurable HDA hardware architecture + codegen targets)
Define scale levels, memory layers, network topo
Compile to any user-defined distributed arch
Hopper CTA cluster NoC peer SM access
L7 - Physical Distributed Systems (hybrid multi-level distributed AI compute)
Multi-scale nested T.Scale - L2 inter-GPU + L1 warpgroup reduce
T.Kernel(device=4, block=(grid_M,grid_N), threads=256) - 4-way tensor parallel launch
T.Scale("device"): T.view global A/B/C with FullCol/FullRow/Replica layouts
T.Scale("block"): pipelined K-loop - T.gemm on l0 tiles - warpgroup T.allreduce on L1
T.Scale("device"): T.allreduce(C_global) on L2 across 4 GPUs via NVLink/NVSHMEM
Compiler overlaps comm+compute - cost model picks TMA/CE impl - lower to CUDA+NVSHMEM
FlashMLA: 4-GPU context parallel - KV sharded by seqlen - warpgroup allgather on acc_s
Design Position + TileScale vs TileLang vs NVIDIA cuTile
TileScale extends TileLang from single-device kernels to hierarchical distributed mega-device
thread -> warp -> warpgroup -> block/SM -> cta_cluster -> device -> node -> ...
Each level: compute group + memory layer access + peer network - unified by T.Scale
Design: first stack unifying intra-chip + inter-chip distributed resources as one programmable mega-device
Sources: github.com/tile-ai/tilescale README - TileLang extension - HDA whitepaper coming soon - NOT NVIDIA cuTile
